next_action.description: Ask Fabio the blocking question before running anything: does the product target SOFT faces (B1 already says GO, restoration branch ships as-is) or WRONG faces (needs section 4 Level 2 - an identity source and a model that will move geometry)? If wrong, the first move is to READ comfy_workflows/raw/flow_head_swap.json plus the LTX2.3 head_swap LoRAs already present in the bench lora enum - reference-conditioned head swap on the LTX-2.3 checkpoint we ship is the nearest existing asset and this card has never looked at it. Do not re-run B2 to test this; re-READ it (it closed LTX as a detailer, explicitly not as an identity carrier).

key_decisions: THE finding, and it reframes the card: restoration fixes SOFTNESS, not WRONGNESS. Source lapvar predicts the result every time - B1 1.7 -> 10.9x restored, B1-stress 1.8 -> 61x, B10 13.5 -> 3.8x. SeedVR2 has no identity source and cannot move geometry (section 4 Level 1), so a sharp-but-wrong face just gets denoised. Fabio's opening complaint - 'small faces lose identity and sometimes look distorted' - is TWO defects and only the first is answered.

B2: SeedVR2 wins on sharpness (10.86x vs 2.45x), identity stability, plastic-ness and VRAM (3.5GB vs a 20GB int8 transformer pinning 15.71/16 GiB). Speed ties warm (30s vs 35s). 0.50 and 0.70 were run beyond the plan's ~0.3 so the loss could not be blamed on a bad sigma schedule.

B2 did NOT close LTX v2v as an identity carrier - only as a detailer. Its willingness to restructure a face at denoise 0.5-0.7, recorded there as 'drift', is exactly the behaviour the wrongness case needs once identity is anchored. Re-read before re-running.
Fabio's correction: MpiFaceWindow needs tracking and multi-face association but NOT shot detection - the user trims to the face shot before handing the clip over.

Fabio supplied a character sheet (t2i_022.png) as an identity asset. It is UNUSABLE on the SeedVR2 branch - SeedVR2Conditioning takes only (model, latent), no reference input. It is a Level 2 asset, held for that question.
constraints: THE BENCH IS UP on 8188 (~40 GB resident, plus the 20 GB LTX transformer from B2 still on the card). KILL IT unless the next session opens with bench work. Bench path is G:\ComfyUi\ComfyUI\ (nested), core 0.31.0.

SILENT GRAPH BUG, and it will bite again: SeedVR2Conditioning must be fed the CHUNKED latent (the SeedVR2TemporalChunk output), not the raw VAEEncodeTiled output. The donor wires ONE MpiIfElse output to both KSampler.latent_image and SeedVR2Conditioning.vae_conditioning. Wired to the unchunked latent it passes validation and every single-chunk run, then dies with 'SeedVR2 conditioning shape must match latent batch/temporal/spatial dimensions'. It survived B1, B1-stress and the whole 512 run undetected.

The laplacian metric has now picked the WRONG winner twice on this card - most starkly at B1-stress, where the branch with the most destroyed face scored the HIGHEST sharpness (60.89x). It measures how blurred the SOURCE was. Use it only as a collapse detector, never to rank. Fabio's eye gates every visual verdict; the plan's verify mode is user-ux.

Before spending a run on any new clip, CHECK THE LANCZOS BASELINE FIRST. If the un-upscaled source face has no eyes, no restoration model can put them back and the run measures nothing - that cost three runs on the 864x480 clip.
Fabio's source files live in an ACTIVE project. Copy to scratchpad before use, never work against Documents\Cubric Vision\Projects\ directly.

Working runner scripts are in this session's scratchpad (run_seedvr2.py is the parametrised B1 graph, run_b2.py the LTX v2v one) but every graph is reconstructable from brief.md, which records both chains node by node.
